review_summary: Question 5 (Modulation and Satellite Communication) verified with PASS across all 6 leaves (a), (b)(i), (b)(ii), (b)(iii), (c)(i), and (c)(ii). Leaf (a) verifies the precise definition of amplitude modulation where the carrier wave amplitude varies in synchrony with (or in proportion to) the displacement of the information signal. Leaf (b)(i) evaluates wavelength lambda = c / f = (3.0 * 10^8) / (900 * 10^3) = 3.3 * 10^2 m (333 m). Leaf (b)(ii) accurately describes continuous amplitude envelope variation between maximum and minimum repeating 5000 times each second (every 0.20 ms) above and below 4.0 V. Leaf (b)(iii) calculates bandwidth = 2 * f_m = 2 * 5.0 kHz = 10000 Hz. Leaf (c)(i) confirms the required features of a geostationary orbit: equatorial orbital plane, west-to-east orbital direction matching Earth's rotation, and circular orbit of specific radius. Leaf (c)(ii) provides physical justifications: GHz waves pass through the atmosphere/ionosphere with minimal absorption/reflection, and different uplink/downlink frequencies prevent the amplified retransmitted downlink signal from swamping the faint incoming uplink signal. All hints, walkthroughs, deterministic checks, rubrics, and taxonomy mappings are fully compliant.
